overall: Atlanta had a significantly cooler-than-expected day on June 23, with the running maximum reaching only 73.9°F — roughly 12°F below the NWS-forecast high of 86°F. Heavy cloud cover throughout the morning (OVC at multiple hours) combined with 0.74 inches of cumulative precipitation dramatically suppressed daytime heating. The daily peak occurred at 17:52 ET and temperatures have been declining since, now at 71.6°F with a slow cooling trend.
forecast_obs_notes: ECMWF (74.2°F) and HRRR (73.5°F) both performed very well, closely bracketing the observed running max of 73.9°F. NBM (79.5°F) overestimated by roughly 5-6°F. The NWS narrative forecast of 86°F was substantially wrong, likely failing to account for the precipitation and persistent cloud cover that dominated the day. All four NWP timing models and the intraday model disagree on peak hour, but this is now moot as the peak is confirmed 4+ hours in the past.
max_temp_prediction: The day is effectively over — at 21:55 ET, temperatures are declining at -0.3°F/hr with light winds and skies clearing to FEW. The running maximum of 73.9°F is locked in as today's TMAX with near-certainty; the intraday model assigns 94.6% probability to the 72-73°F bucket (consistent with 73.9°F), and no mechanism exists for temperatures to rebound above that level overnight. Confidence is extremely high.
